comments.text: Liberia isn't a settler colony, that's a lie further enforced by Wikipedia. Historical sources don't mention any colonialist proof and those that do are either falsified and far from being primary sources like the false account about Robert Stockton forcing King Peter at gunpoint. When the native kings were asked if they wanted to join France or US-Afro-Americans they opted almost unaminously for the latter. Only after the US invasion of Liberia in 1989 was there dissent among Nativo-Liberians and US-Americo-Liberians, in fact, native Liberians actually made up the 50% of teachers. You all should read "Liberia & the Quest for Freedom: The Half That Has Never Been Told", "Citizenship & Nationality in Liberia" and the original Liberian constitution. 14.00 'After independence’ (only after? ok maybe). In Africa, SubSaharan centres of civilization had their own alphabets / writing systems before Europe had literacy* 
To mention *some* examples of the African alphabets / writing sytems: Nsibidi from the western coast near Liberia (Nigeria-Camaroon region) and all the way across to the east of the continent with scripts like Meriotic (Sudan region) and Ge’ez (Ethiopia). The Nsibidi writing system developed independently and is between 1,400 and over 2,000 years old, and still in use today. Meriotic 2,300 years ago. Ge’ez 2,500 years old and still in use today.

*Europe doesn’t have its own alphabets except for perhaps Ogham, but then the Celts came from Anatolia / Parthia in Asia. Runes the Germanics took from the Iberian Celts and or Turkic nations, Greeks took the idea of alphabet from the Phonecians in Asia). Literacy was out of reach of the majoririty of ordinary Europeans (+ Eur descendants), having been reserved exclusively for royalty and priests, until about 170 years ago.
